title: dependency-model:synthesis contract
description: The envelope `synthesize` emits: the merged discovery inventory plus the graph and health view derived from it. report, #50, and #51 consume this. Judgment about which conditions matter belongs to those consumers, not to this contract.

target.description: Absolute path of the repository this was synthesized from.

ref.description: The git ref this was synthesized from, as depscan.py --ref recorded it. Absent or null means the working tree, uncommitted edits included.

name.description: The ref as given, e.g. main.

commit.description: The commit SHA it resolved to.

components.description: The system's own first-party components, copied from the profile:topology contract's components[] with an id added. They are what the inventory's dependencies are depended on by, so they are graph nodes (category `component`) and health anchors, but never inventory entries. Absent or empty when no topology was supplied.

id.description: 'component:<slug>', the slug rule in references/categories.md (Ids) applied to the topology component's name.

inventory.description: The discovery envelopes for this target, merged by key union across whichever discovery skills ran.

graph.description: The dependency graph derived from the inventory: one node per discovered dependency, one per first-party component, one edge per relationship between them.

id.description: Same id as the corresponding inventory dependency, '<category>:<slug>'; or a components[] id.

category.description: The inventory category, or `component` for a first-party component from components[] -- not a dependency, so it has no inventory entry.

lifecycle.description: Always run for a component node: the component is the running thing.

kind.description: depends_on: one dependency requires another to function, e.g. a package's transitive dependency. relates_to: two dependencies are the same real-world thing seen from different categories, e.g. a service and the network port that reaches it -- the correlation `related_ids` already carries, made explicit as an edge.

lifecycle.description: The source node's (`from`) lifecycle, propagated onto the edge -- not a constant per `kind`. A package depended on only at build time produces a `build` edge; one that ships at runtime produces `run`, whatever the edge's `kind`.

cycles.description: Each entry is a list of node ids forming one cycle in the depends_on graph. Empty when none were found.

health.description: One entry per anchor -- a `run` service, or a first-party component -- that carries failure-relevant conditions, gathered from the inventory's resilience facts and related dependencies. No entry means no conditions were found, not that the anchor is fine.

service_id.description: The graph node id this health entry describes: a `run` service ('service:<slug>') or a first-party component ('component:<slug>', from components[]). The field name predates component anchors and is kept for compatibility.

kind.description: presence: subject_id must exist/resolve, e.g. a network path or a config key. bound: subject_id carries a declared limit, e.g. a timeout or retry count. upstream_health: subject_id's own health entry feeds this one, e.g. a service that depends on another service. Uniform on purpose: a consumer that ANDed two special-cased lists (a 'requires' list and a 'bounds' list) would be encoding a met/unmet-AND-within/outside binary that real systems don't have a middle for. That vocabulary is deliberately not defined here -- see the contract's no-state-vocabulary rule.

subject_id.description: The id this condition is about -- a graph node id, or another identifier the evidence points at.

expectation.description: The declaration found in the repository, or null. null means no declaration was found -- it never means no bound is needed. Whether an unbounded request-path dependency is a real gap is a judgment for a later layer, not this contract.

required_for.description: Ids of the components ('component:<slug>', from components[]) or functions that need this condition met, from static evidence. Records which callers depend on it, never how important any of them are; may be empty when no caller could be established.

evidence.description: Locations that prove this condition exists, as 'file:line'.
